Ok so I just moved into an apartment and one of my roomates isn't like SUPER rich, but she grew up alot more well off than the rest of us did. It seems like she has a MUCH different taste in foods than us. I've never met anybody that absolutely hated the taste of taco bell like she does, and she was equally weirded out that we thought her tuna fish with grapes was weird as hell. I just cooked canned pinto beans on the stove, and I swear she looked like she wanted to slap me. Even their potato salad tasted bland to me, but she insisted that it was amazing. Is this a widespread thing, or is this just because we happen to have different tastes?
Why do 'poor people' hate 'rich people' food? And vice versa

I would say, no this isn’t really a widespread thing relating to social status – it’s more people’s upbringing and how their palates developed as they aged. I know plenty of people who are extremely well off who still love the taste of McDonalds. Not because they fall into a certain socio-economic category, but because either their parents allowed them to eat fast food (or vice-versa, and they actively sought out unhealthy food due to constraints imposed by their parents.) I would say socio-economic condition only exists as the most basic starting point for explaining this behavior. It has much more to do with progression of taste while maturing and parenting style.

Based on comparisons between people I know who are tight on money and people who have money to burn...

People who are tight on money are more concerned with getting enough caloric value out of their food to keep them running during the day. Fast food might be shit for your health, but it doesn't cost much on a per calorie basis, which is what you need to survive.

People who are flush with money are more likely to not care exactly how much they are spending on food, and instead are interested in "exotic" flavors and ingredients. They are more likely to visit "hipster" restaurants or Whole Foods grocery stores, and don't care how much their food costs as long as they can talk about how it's a "superfood" or "organic".

"Poor people" hate the fact that "rich people" food costs too much for them to be able to afford enough of it to live on, and "rich people" hate "poor people" food because it isn't particularly healthy.

Ya this seems to answer it pretty well. She is the type of person that likes mores exotic food, like the tunafish and grapes I guess. And being on a pretty tight budget, even tighter than usual now, fast food is at least 50 percent of all my meals.
I don't know if /v/eatcheapandhealthy is a thing yet, but with very little effort, you can spend way less than you do on fast food and get better grub.
I think it just depends on the environment you grew up in coupled with whether of not you were raised to be accepting or open minded to things you do not understand or aren't accustomed to.
